stories.title: Foreign Delegates Arrive in Islamabad for 30th ECO Ministerial Meeting
stories.summary:
High-level delegates from friendly and regional nations began arriving in Islamabad on Sunday to participate in the 30th Economic Cooperation Organisation Council of Ministers meeting. The two-day conference, scheduled for November 15 to 16, aims to enhance regional connectivity and integration under the leadership of Pakistan, which holds the ECO chair for 2026-2027 with the theme "Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO."

Among the arrivals welcomed at the airport by foreign ministry officials were Turkish Deputy Foreign Minister Musa Kulaklikaya, Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Deputy Secretary General Ahmad Saidmurodzoda, Organisation of Islamic Cooperation Secretary General Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed, Azerbaijani Deputy Foreign Minister Elnur Mammadov, and Kazakh Deputy Foreign Minister Arman Issagaliyev. Additionally, Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus Foreign Minister Tahsin Ertuğruloğlu reached the federal capital a day prior.

The ministerial huddle will be chaired by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and attended by foreign ministers, delegation heads, and ECO secretariat representatives. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is also expected to attend amid ongoing Middle East conflict mediation efforts involving Pakistan and Qatar.

The main ministerial gathering follows a Meeting of Senior Officials. This preparatory session reviewed organizational programs, evaluated subsidiary bodies, and finalized the agenda and draft outcome documents for consideration by the council members.

stories.title: National Assembly Session Expected to Be Postponed, Sources Say
stories.summary:
The upcoming National Assembly session is likely to be rescheduled after Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has not yet sent a formal summary to President Asif Ali Zardari to summon the meeting. Parliamentary sources indicate that the session, initially proposed by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs to convene on Monday at 5:00 PM, is now expected to take place next week following discussions between the president and the prime minister.

The postponement decision followed a detailed meeting in Lahore's Model Town, where President Zardari and Prime Minister Sharif reviewed the nation's political, economic, and security situation. The premier briefed the president on his recent participation in the 31st Conference of Parties in Turkiye regarding climate action. Both leaders also discussed allied party cooperation, ongoing public welfare projects, and reaffirmed their shared commitment to accelerating economic stability and development.

Several key figures attended the meeting, including National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq Khan, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, political affairs adviser Rana Sanaullah, former prime minister Raja Pervez Ashraf, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla, and Mna Hamza Shehbaz.

The consultation comes shortly after Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met with President Zardari. The President House previously clarified that their discussion focused on national security and the regional situation rather than the formation of new provinces.

stories.title: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Wildlife Department Permits Partridge Hunting in Reserves
stories.summary:
The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Wildlife Department has issued a formal notification authorizing partridge hunting in designated game reserves across the province. The hunting season is scheduled to run from November 15, 2026, to January 11, 2027, applying exclusively to areas officially declared open by the government.

Under the new guidelines, hunters are permitted to target four specific bird species: the Chukar partridge, Black partridge, Grey partridge, and See-See partridge. Participation is strictly restricted to individuals who possess both a valid shooting licence and a special hunting permit issued by the department. Hunting without these official credentials remains strictly prohibited across all provincial reserves.

To safeguard local wildlife populations, the department will continuously monitor partridge numbers within the designated game reserves. Authorities have noted that the ongoing issuance of special permits could be suspended if population statuses warrant conservation interventions.

This announcement follows a previous decision by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government to lift the ban on quail hunting. Under official order number 58, Chief Conservator of Wildlife authorized the hunting of common and rain quails for licensed individuals, setting a strict daily bag limit of eight quails per hunter while directing personnel to strictly enforce regulations.

stories.title: Pakistani Leaders Share Top Spot in 2025 Most Influential Muslims List
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir have shared the top rank in the latest edition of "The 500 Most Influential Muslims." Compiled annually by the Amman-based Royal Islamic Strategic Studies Centre since 2009, the publication shares the premier position with Saudi King and Crown Prince and the Turkish President, marking the first time multiple individuals have claimed the top spot.

The historic recognition stems from the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye. The mutual-defense pact combines Saudi wealth, Turkish technology, and Pakistani military strength into a collective alliance modeled on a "one for all, all for one" security framework that reshapes regional politics. The report also praised Pakistan's diplomatic balancing acts, economic stabilization challenges, and maintenance of strategic ties with Riyadh alongside communication channels with Tehran.

Other notable figures in the rankings include Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei at fourth, Jordan's King Abdullah II at fifth, and Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al-Thani at sixth. Prominent Pakistani scholar Sheikh Muhammad Taqi Usmani is ranked seventh, while Maulana Tariq Jamil is placed 32nd. Former prime minister Imran Khan received an honorable mention in politics.

Additionally, the institute named Palestinian paediatrician Dr Hussam Abu Safiya as Man of the Year for his endurance in Gaza's health infrastructure, while Minab school attack survivor Fatemeh Zahra Sheikhabadi was honored as Woman of the Year after addressing the UN Human Rights Council.

stories.title: Section 144 Imposed Across Bannu District Amid Security Concerns
stories.summary:
Authorities have enforced Section 144 throughout the Bannu district to safeguard law and order, banning public gatherings and protest rallies for a period of one month. The restrictive measures also strictly prohibit blocking roads, creating hurdles, displaying arms and ammunition, pillion riding, and utilizing tinted glasses across the region.

This decision follows a recent counter-terrorism operation in which Peshawar police thwarted an assault by Fitna al-Khawarij on a police check post located at the Bannu Kangar bridge. According to the City Police Officer (CPO), four terrorists belonging to the group were killed during the nighttime clash, and authorities recovered arms and ammunition from their possession. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Inspector General (IG) praised the police force for their valor, emphasizing that there is no tolerance for terrorists on provincial soil and that their total eradication will be pursued.

The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) previously reported that 74 khwarij linked to the Indian-sponsored Fitna-al-Khawarij were eliminated during security operations across Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Meanwhile, in Islamabad, parliamentary sources indicate that an upcoming National Assembly session is likely to be rescheduled. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has not yet submitted the required summary to President Asif Ali Zardari to officially summon the session, despite an earlier proposal forwarded by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.

The enforcement of Section 144 and ongoing counter-terrorism operations highlight the government's heightened security posture in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. These measures aim to curb public disturbances and neutralize militant threats, ensuring greater stability for residents in the affected districts during a critical period of legislative and security adjustments.

stories.title: US Air Travel Disruptions Expected to Persist Until Sunday Night
stories.summary:
United States aviation authorities anticipate that air travel will not return to normal schedules until late Sunday evening. The ongoing delays and cancellations stem from a nationwide ground stop ordered by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) after a routine maintenance upgrade caused widespread disruptions to air traffic communications and radar systems.

According to the aviation tracking website FlightAware, airlines cancelled over 6,400 US flights and delayed more than 8,000 following a Friday ground stop that halted nearly all departing flights for almost five hours. This marked the longest nationwide aviation halt since the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy explained that the chaos began when maintenance work involving the replacement of old copper wire with a high-speed fiber cable caused data overloading across 17 of the FAA’s 22 en route centres. The issue was traced to router updates performed by FAA contractor L3Harris at a remote facility.

FAA head Bryan Bedford offered a sincere apology to the traveling public during a news conference, predicting that normal operations would resume by the close of business on Sunday. Major carriers such as Delta Air Lines, United Airlines, and American Airlines cancelled roughly 25 percent of their flights on Saturday, while JetBlue cancelled nearly 45 percent, leaving hundreds of thousands of passengers stranded in airports nationwide. Airlines have responded by issuing travel waivers allowing passengers to rebook flights without additional costs.

The incident has renewed scrutiny on the ageing infrastructure of the US air traffic control system. Transportation Secretary Duffy called for $50 billion in funding to modernize the system, drawing support from Republican House Speaker Mike Johnson and criticism from Democratic officials over past spending. Meanwhile, congressional panels plan to hold the administration accountable to prevent similar chaos in the future.

stories.title: قومی اسمبلی کا اجلاس مؤخر، وزیراعظم اور صدر کی ملاقات میں فیصلہ
stories.summary:
وزیر اعظم شہباز شریف نے قومی اسمبلی کا اجلاس کل بلانے کی سمری ابھی تک صدر کو ارسال نہیں کی ہے۔ پارلیمانی ذرائع کا کہنا ہے کہ وزارت پارلیمانی امور نے پیر کے روز شام 5 بجے اجلاس طلب کرنے کی سمری وزیراعظم کو بھیجی تھی۔

ذرائع کے مطابق صدر مملکت اور وزیراعظم کے درمیان ہونے والی ملاقات میں یہ فیصلہ کیا گیا ہے کہ قومی اسمبلی کے اس اجلاس کو اب ری شیڈول کیا جائے۔ اس باہمی مشاورت کے بعد اب یہ اجلاس آئندہ ہفتے طلب کیے جانے کا قوی امکان ظاہر کیا جا رہا ہے۔

اس تبدیلی سے متعلق پارلیمانی حلقوں میں تیاریاں اور مشاورت جاری ہے۔ اجلاس کی نئی تاریخ کا باضابطہ اعلان جلد متوقع ہے تاکہ تمام اراکین پارلیمنٹ کو بروقت اطلاع دی جا سکے۔

stories.title: گوجرانوالہ میں بیوی کو بلیک میل کرنے والا شوہر گرفتار
stories.summary:
گوجرانوالہ میں اپنی بیوی کو قابلِ اعتراض ڈیٹا کے ذریعے بلیک میل اور ہراساں کرنے والے ملزم کو گرفتار کر لیا گیا ہے۔ نیشنل سائبر کانگریس انوسٹی گیشن ایجنسی کے ترجمان کے مطابق خاتون کی شکایت پر یہ کارروائی عمل میں لائی گئی۔

ترجمان نے بتایا کہ گرفتار ملزم کے موبائل فون سے غیر اخلاقی ڈیٹا برآمد ہوا ہے، جس پر اس کے خلاف باقاعدہ مقدمہ درج کر لیا گیا ہے۔ فیصل آباد میں بھی ایک اور کارروائی کے دوران تصاویر ہٹانے کے عوض 5 لاکھ روپے بھتہ مانگنے والے شخص کو دبوچا گیا ہے۔

عورت کی جانب سے فوری شکایت درج کرانے کے بعد این سی سی آئی اے نے فوری ایکشن لیا۔ ان کارروائیوں کا مقصد ڈیجیٹل پلیٹ فارمز کے ذریعے خواتین کو نشانہ بنانے والے عناصر کے خلاف گھیرا تنگ کرنا ہے۔

stories.title: Netanyahu Calls for Unity Government as Eisenkot Rejects Tricks
stories.summary:
Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has reiterated his calls for a national unity government with his political opponent, Gadi Eisenkot, who promptly dismissed the proposal as a political ruse. Netanyahu argued in a video statement that a unity government is essential for national security and to eliminate the Iranian threat, warning against Eisenkot's alternative plan to form a minority government backed by abstentions from Arab and ultra-Orthodox lawmakers.

Eisenkot, who was tapped last Sunday to form a new government within 28 days, rejected the appeal, stating that Netanyahu knows he lost the election and is engaging in political tricks. The former army chief criticized Netanyahu for sowing division and running a racist campaign against Arab-Israeli parties, which secured a record number of seats in the recent election. Eisenkot indicated he is open to partnerships with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party and Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism under conditions of sincere commitment to unity, but ruled out a coalition with Netanyahu himself and demanded a break with far-right extremists like Itamar Ben Gvir's supporters.

Another major point of contention centers on the upcoming Tuesday election for the speaker of the Knesset. The opposition has nominated Matan Kahana, a former army officer running on Eisenkot's list, to replace the current speaker and Netanyahu ally, Amir Ohana. Eisenkot insisted that if Likud and its allies truly seek a sincere political partnership, they must permit the democratic process to proceed normally and instruct their parliamentarians to support Kahana's appointment.

The ongoing political deadlock highlights deep divisions within the Israeli parliament as negotiations continue. With Eisenkot holding a limited window to secure a coalition, the path forward remains fraught with ideological disagreements over government composition, leadership roles, and the inclusion or exclusion of specific political factions.

stories.title: Eisenkot Dismisses Netanyahu's Unity Government Call As a Ruse
stories.summary:
Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu urged opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to join a national unity government during a video statement released on Saturday. Netanyahu maintained that a broad coalition is vital to guarantee national security and permanently eliminate the threat posed by Iran. He cautioned against Eisenkot's pursuit of a minority government, which would rely on abstentions from 26 Arab and ultra-Orthodox lawmakers to pass in the 120-seat Knesset without securing an absolute majority.

Eisenkot swiftly rejected the overture, accusing Netanyahu of playing political tricks despite knowing he lost the election. The former military chief asserted that Netanyahu's public appeals for unity contradict his ongoing efforts to stoke division and discredit Arab-Israeli parties, which achieved record representation in the recent vote. Eisenkot was tasked last Sunday with forming a government within 28 days, a process that includes a potential 14-day extension and presents significant negotiation challenges.

While Eisenkot remains open to governing with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party and Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism contingent upon a genuine commitment to unity, he firmly ruled out partnering with Netanyahu directly. He also conditioned any participation on distancing the administration from extremists aligned with far-right minister Itamar Ben Gvir, pointing to Netanyahu's campaign rhetoric as racially divisive.

An immediate test of political cooperation involves the upcoming Tuesday vote for the Knesset speaker. The opposition has put forward Matan Kahana to replace incumbent speaker Amir Ohana, a close ally of Netanyahu. Eisenkot stated that if Likud and its allies genuinely desire a sincere political partnership, they must allow normal democratic procedures to unfold and instruct their parliamentarians to support Kahana's bid.

stories.title: ناروے کی صحافی کا ویزا منسوخ، انڈین وزارتِ داخلہ کے احکامات کا دعویٰ
stories.summary:
ناروے کی صحافی ہیلا لینگ نے دعویٰ کیا ہے کہ حیدرآباد میں منعقد ہونے والی 'بھارت سمٹ' میں شرکت کے لیے حاصل کردہ ان کا ویزا وزارتِ داخلہ کے احکامات پر آخری وقت میں منسوخ کر دیا گیا۔ انھیں میڈیا کے مستقبل اور صحافتی آزادی پر پینل مباحثے میں شریک ہونا تھا۔

یہ کانفرنس 13 اور 14 نومبر کو تلنگانہ حکومت اور سمردھی بھارت فاؤنڈیشن کے اشتراک سے منعقد ہوئی۔ ہیلا لینگ کے مطابق مئی 2026 میں اوسلو میں انڈین وزیراعظم نریندر مودی سے سوال پوچھنے پر تنقید اور مضامین کی وجہ سے یہ سیاسی فیصلہ کیا گیا۔ کانگریس کا دعویٰ ہے کہ 116 غیر ملکی مندوبین کو بھی داخلے سے روکا گیا۔

انڈین وزارتِ خارجہ کے ترجمان رندھیر جیسوال نے مؤقف اپنایا کہ ویزا جاری کرنا یا مسترد کرنا ہر حکومت کا خودمختار اختیار ہے۔ دوسری جانب، کانگریس رہنما سلمان خورشید اور منتظم پشپ راج دیشپانڈے نے غیر ملکی مندوبین کو درپیش مشکلات پر تشویش کا اظہار کرتے ہوئے حکومت سے وضاحت کا مطالبہ کیا ہے۔

stories.title: IMF Urges Pakistan to Phase Out Petrol Subsidy Program
stories.summary:
The International Monetary Fund has formally requested that Pakistan gradually eliminate its current fuel support program. According to an IMF spokesperson speaking with Arab News, any future fuel assistance needs to be strictly limited, targeted, and time-bound, and must be accommodated within the budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year. The directive stems from a staff-level agreement reached on October 7, with the organization pointing out that the existing mechanism features a broad targeting system. Under the current initiative introduced in September, low-income motorcycle and rickshaw operators receive weekly petrol vouchers valued at 500 rupees, while vehicles with engine sizes up to 800cc obtain a discount of 100 rupees per litre. This policy is part of broader economic recovery steps tied to Pakistan's $7 billion loan arrangement with the fund.

Alongside the subsidy phase-out, Islamabad has committed to syncing domestic petroleum prices with international market figures. The spokesperson noted that ongoing conflicts in the Middle East present a significant challenge for the country, which depends heavily on Gulf nations for gas and oil imports. Surging global oil costs have pushed domestic inflation levels upward, registering at 9.6 percent in October following a 10.3 percent rate in September. The international financial body cautioned that persistent global oil price fluctuations could jeopardize the nation's economic trajectory.

To safeguard its economic outlook, the organization underscored the necessity for Pakistan to uphold macroeconomic stability alongside carrying out structural reforms in state-owned enterprises and enhancing the energy sector. An upcoming meeting of the IMF Executive Board is anticipated to occur in December to review ongoing developments. In separate domestic political developments within Islamabad, parliamentary sources indicated that the upcoming National Assembly session is likely to face rescheduling. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has not yet transmitted the required summary to President Asif Ali Zardari to formally summon the legislative gathering, even though the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs had previously forwarded a proposal to convene the session.

stories.title: Saudi Coalition Intercepts Ballistic Missiles and Drones Targeting Kingdom
stories.summary:
The military coalition led by Saudi Arabia fighting Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement announced that it successfully intercepted two ballistic missiles directed at the Saudi capital of Riyadh. In addition to the capital-bound projectiles, the alliance neutralized three drones aimed at the kingdom's oil-abundant Eastern Province. These incidents reflect an escalation in cross-border strikes against strategic locations within Saudi territory by the Houthis, who maintain control over the majority of populated regions in Yemen.

The recent surge in assaults includes an incident from the prior week where a Houthi strike inflicted damage upon an administrative building belonging to state oil giant Saudi Aramco located in Riyadh's financial district. Meanwhile, the Eastern Province remains a frequent target for aerial attacks due to its status as the nation's economic powerhouse. The region holds the vast majority of Saudi Arabia's oil and gas reserves and serves as the base for Aramco headquarters, which suffered extensive destruction during a previous attack in October.

Over recent weeks, the Houthi movement has intensified offensive operations targeting various Saudi infrastructure installations, including domestic ports, airports, and oil facilities. In retaliation to these persistent aerial incursions, Saudi Arabia has significantly escalated its own campaign of airstrikes targeting Houthi positions inside Yemen. The ongoing military exchanges highlight the deepening conflict between the neighboring adversaries and the continuous threat posed to critical energy infrastructure in the region.

stories.title: PPP and IPP Candidates Face Off in Gilgit-Baltistan Repolling
stories.summary:
Voting is taking place under tight security in Gilgit for the GBA-16 (Diamer-II) seat, featuring a renewed electoral contest between Attaullah Shah of the Pakistan Peoples Party and Imam Malik of the Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party. A total of 2,780 registered voters are eligible to participate, with polling scheduled to conclude at 5 pm.

Malik originally contested the June elections as an independent candidate before joining the IPP and being initially declared the winner by the election commission. However, his membership was suspended in September following a petition by Shah, which argued that the returning officer issued Form-49 without counting postal ballots. An election tribunal subsequently ordered verification, leading to Shah being declared the victor on September 14 by a narrow margin of 13 votes after securing 6,618 votes.

Following this, Malik challenged the tribunal's verdict at the GB Supreme Appellate Court, which upheld Shah's status as the returned candidate on September 19. Malik then petitioned the election tribunal again to request fresh voting at three specific polling stations. The tribunal accepted this request, suspended Shah's membership, and mandated that the chief election commissioner conduct repolling at those three stations within 12 days of November 6.

stories.title: Chelsea Defeats Manchester City to Claim Women's Super League Lead
stories.summary:
Chelsea secured a 1-0 victory over defending champions Manchester City, handing them their first defeat of the Women's Super League season and moving to the top of the league table. The match leaves Chelsea with 26 points from 10 matches, putting them one point ahead of second-placed City after the same number of games.

The game's only goal occurred during first-half stoppage time when Sandy Baltimore received a pass on the right side of the penalty area, turned, and shot past goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita. Chelsea midfielder Keira Walsh noted an improvement in team intensity, stating that winning first and second balls dictated the outcome of the fixture.

Manchester City's chances of maintaining their unbeaten status diminished further in the 75th minute when Yamashita received a red card for rushing outside her penalty box and colliding with Chelsea forward Alyssa Thompson. Eartha Cumings substituted for Yamashita as City finished the match with 10 players, while Chelsea's Aggie Beever-Jones hit the crossbar with a second-half free kick before the hosts preserved their lead.

In other Women's Super League matches, Manchester United defeated Crystal Palace 2-0 with goals from Maya Le Tissier and Elisabeth Terland, placing United fourth with 18 points. Tottenham Hotspur drew 0-0 with Everton, and Liverpool defeated Brighton & Hove Albion 3-0 through goals from Beata Olsson and Cornelia Kapocs.

stories.title: Aryna Sabalenka Issues Apology for Outburst During WTA Finals Match
stories.summary:
Aryna Sabalenka issued an apology for an angry outburst that occurred during her defeat against Ukraine's Elina Svitolina at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells. Television footage from Friday's round-robin match appeared to show the Belarusian player swearing, leading social media users to believe the remarks were directed at Svitolina or Ukrainians. The loss resulted in Sabalenka's elimination from the tournament.

Clarifying the incident on social media, Sabalenka stated that her comments were aimed at a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering her mistakes rather than at Elina Svitolina. She acknowledged reacting too emotionally and expressed regret for any offense caused, while praising Svitolina for playing a great match and wishing her well.

Following the match, Svitolina did not shake hands with Sabalenka, maintaining her policy regarding Russian and Belarusian opponents that began after Russia's 2002 invasion of Ukraine, which used Belarus as a staging ground. When asked about the apology, Svitolina emphasized the need for mutual respect and noted that fans' passions can run high, adding that she hopes future matches between them will be respected despite past negative comments regarding the war. Svitolina advanced to face Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva in the final.

stories.title: ASEAN to Maintain Engagement With Myanmar, Says Philippine President
stories.summary:
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations has agreed to sustain its constructive and principled engagement with Myanmar, according to Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. The announcement was made on Sunday during the annual ASEAN summit hosted in Manila.

President Marcos Jr., who is chairing the regional bloc's summit, stated his hope that the organization can successfully advance the implementation of its established five-point peace plan for Myanmar. The diplomatic approach comes as ASEAN continues to navigate a complex dilemma regarding the country, with some member states pursuing closer ties.

stories.title: Mirra Andreeva Reaches WTA Finals Championship Match Against Elina Svitolina
stories.summary:
Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva advanced to the WTA Finals championship match by defeating American Jessica Pegula 6-3, 6-4 in the tournament's semi-finals. Playing in the California desert under sunny skies, Andreeva relied on heavy groundstrokes, strong serving, and tireless defense during their first career meeting. The opening set remained tight until Andreeva broke serve for a 5-3 lead and capitalized on Pegula's errors. Although Pegula grabbed an early advantage in the second set, Andreeva quickly fought back with successive breaks to secure the victory. Making her tournament debut, Andreeva has not dropped a single set across four matches at the event.

She will face sixth seed Elina Svitolina in Sunday's final after the Ukrainian defeated Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova 6-2, 6-1 in just over an hour. Svitolina raced to a commanding lead in the second set to seal her spot in the title match. She has reached the final in all three of her appearances at the eight-player championships, having previously won the title in 2018.

While Andreeva holds a 2-1 lead in their head-to-head matchups, including a 6-4, 6-0 round-robin victory earlier in the week, Svitolina noted that she has significantly elevated her level of play since then. The tournament, carrying a $10 million prize pool, was relocated from Riyadh to the Indian Wells Tennis Garden due to the US-Israeli war with Iran.

stories.title: Portugal Suffers 4-1 Defeat to Denmark After Cristiano Ronaldo's Retirement
stories.summary:
Portugal suffered a heavy 4-1 home defeat against Denmark in the Nations League in Braga, marking their first match since Cristiano Ronaldo announced his international retirement. Ahead of the fixture, Portuguese players wore shirts bearing Ronaldo's name and number seven during the national anthem, while supporters displayed a banner thanking the former captain, who stepped down following a public dispute with manager Jorge Jesus.

Despite dominating possession during a rain-soaked first half, Portugal conceded just before halftime when a penalty was awarded following a VAR review and successfully converted by Denmark captain Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg. Rasmus Hojlund extended Denmark's lead shortly after the break with a powerful volley, and added a third goal minutes later on a counter-attack. Joachim Andersen further cemented the victory with a towering header in the 75th minute before Bernardo Silva scored a late consolation goal for Portugal in added time.

In the group's other fixture, Norway defeated Wales 3-1 in Oslo. Antonio Nusa opened the scoring in the second half before Andreas Schjelderup doubled the lead. Although David Brooks temporarily narrowed the deficit for Wales, Erling Haaland secured Norway's win by converting a late penalty in the 88th minute following a foul on Schjelderup.

Following these matches, Portugal remains at the top of League A Group Four with 12 points, three points ahead of Denmark. Norway holds six points and Wales sits at the bottom with three points. The final round of league-phase matches is scheduled for Tuesday, with Wales hosting Portugal and Denmark welcoming Norway.

stories.title: Israel and Hamas Confirm Death of Senior Commander Samir Abu Younis in Gaza Strike
stories.summary:
Hamas announced that Samir Abu Younis, a senior commander who helped plan and oversee the October 7, 2023, attack on Israel, was killed in an Israeli airstrike, a statement confirmed by the Israeli military. The 53-year-old leader of the Rafah brigade was targeted in a street in the Mawasi area of Khan Younis in the southern Gaza Strip. Medics reported that several other individuals were wounded in the same overnight strike.

The Israeli military stated that Abu Younis had commanded the Rafah brigade since September 15, following the death of his predecessor, Nael Abu Obeid. According to Hamas, Abu Younis joined the group's armed wing in 1991 and held multiple operational roles in Rafah over the decades. His funeral was scheduled to take place in Khan Younis on Sunday afternoon.

This incident follows an October 2025 ceasefire that halted major hostilities in the ongoing conflict but failed to stop Israeli military operations or achieve the disarmament of Hamas. Gaza health authorities report that at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began, alongside five Israeli soldier fatalities. The broader military campaign was launched after Hamas-led fighters killed approximately 1,200 people in southern Israel on October 7, resulting in a Palestinian death toll exceeding 74,000 according to local authorities.

stories.title: Dignitaries Arrive in Islamabad for the 30th ECO Council of Ministers Meeting
stories.summary:
Foreign dignitaries have arrived in Islamabad for the commencement of the two-day 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers. Among the prominent officials welcomed by Foreign Office representatives are Turkish Deputy Foreign Minister Musa Kulaklikaya, Azeri Deputy Foreign Minister Elnur Mammadov, and Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Deputy Secretary General Ahmad Saidmurodzoda. Additionally, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus Tahsin Ertugruloglu arrived in the capital to join the discussions.

The ministerial meeting will be chaired by Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar. It will feature foreign ministers, delegation heads from ECO member states, and representatives from the organisation's secretariat and subsidiary bodies. Prior to the ministerial gathering, senior officials convened to review ongoing activities, evaluate subsidiary programs, and finalize agenda items and draft outcome documents.

Pakistan holds the ECO chairmanship for the 2026-27 period and is advancing regional goals under the theme 'Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO'. The Foreign Office stated that Pakistan's leadership aims to prioritize regional connectivity, integration, and economic collaboration to build a logistics hub and shape supply chain logistics. The ECO currently includes Pakistan, Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Tajikistan, Iran, Turkiye, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, the Kyrgyz Republic, and Uzbekistan.

stories.title: باجوڑ میں امن و امان کے پیش نظر دفعہ 144 نافذ
stories.summary:
ضلع باجوڑ میں امن و امان کی مجموعی صورتحال کو بہتر بنانے کے لیے دفعہ 144 نافذ کر دی گئی ہے۔ ڈپٹی کمشنر عدنان فرید کے جاری کردہ حکم کے مطابق یہ پابندی 15 نومبر سے 15 دسمبر تک نافذ العمل رہے گی۔

اس دفعہ کے تحت ضلع بھر میں ہر قسم کے سیاسی اجتماعات پر مکمل پابندی عائد کی گئی ہے۔ اس کے علاوہ پانچ یا اس سے زائد افراد کے جمع ہونے، اسلحہ، ڈنڈے اور پیٹرول بم لے کر چلنے پر بھی قدغن لگائی گئی ہے۔

انتظامیہ کی جانب سے موٹر سائیکل کی ڈبل سواری، لاؤڈ اسپیکر کے استعمال، نفرت انگیز تقاریر اور اسلحے کی نمائش پر بھی پابندی ہوگی۔ ڈپٹی کمشنر نے واضح کیا ہے کہ ان احکامات کی خلاف ورزی کرنے والوں کے خلاف سخت قانونی کارروائی عمل میں لائی جائے گی۔

stories.title: وزیراعظم شہباز شریف اور فیلڈ مارشل عاصم منیر بااثر مسلم شخصیات میں شامل
stories.summary:
اُردن کے رائل اسلامک اسٹریٹجک اسٹڈیز سینٹر کی جانب سے جاری کردہ دنیا کی 500 بااثر مسلم شخصیات کی فہرست کے 2027ء ایڈیشن میں وزیراعظم شہباز شریف اور فیلڈ مارشل عاصم منیر کو شامل کر لیا گیا ہے۔ اس اشاعت کے اٹھارہویں سالانہ ایڈیشن میں پہلی بار پانچ عالمی رہنماؤں کو مشترکہ طور پر پہلی پوزیشن دی گئی ہے۔

اس فہرست کے خصوصی مضمون اور تصاویر میں سعودی قیادت، پاکستانی قیادت اور ترکیہ کے صدر رجب طیب اردوان کو مشترکہ پہلی پوزیشن پر رکھا گیا ہے۔ ابتدائی چارٹ میں سعودی قیادت کو نمبر ایک، پاکستانی قیادت کو نمبر دو اور ترک صدر کو نمبر تین پر درج کیا گیا ہے۔

اس کے علاوہ فہرست میں ایرانی سپریم لیڈر مجتبیٰ خامنہ ای چوتھے، اردن کے فرمانروا شاہ عبداللّٰہ دوم پانچویں اور قطر کے امیر شیخ تمیم بن حمد آل ثانی چھٹے نمبر پر ہیں۔ پاکستان کے معروف عالم دین مفتی محمد تقی عثمانی کو ساتویں پوزیشن دی گئی ہے۔

اس فہرست میں دیگر شخصیات میں ملائیشیا کے وزیراعظم انور ابراہیم تیرہویں اور انڈونیشیا کے صدر پرابووو سوبیانتو سولہویں نمبر پر شامل ہیں۔ ادارے کے مطابق اس فیصلے کی بنیادی وجہ مکہ مشترکہ دفاعی معاہدہ قرار دی گئی ہے۔

stories.title: Israeli Strike Kills Senior Hamas Commander Samir Abu Younis in Gaza
stories.summary:
The Israeli military announced that its forces, along with the internal security agency Shin Bet, struck and killed Samir Abu Younis, a high-ranking military leader within Hamas. According to a joint statement, the strike occurred in the early hours, following his death the previous evening in an operation in Al-Mawasi, located west of Khan Younis. The Islamist movement's Al-Qassam Brigade confirmed the death of Younis, who served as the commander of the brigade's Rafah Brigade and was identified as a key planner of the October 7, 2023 attacks against Israel.

Mahmoud Bassal, the spokesman for Gaza’s civil defence, stated that the agency received the body of the 53-year-old commander, noting that two other individuals sustained injuries during the southern Gaza strike. The Al-Qassam Brigade condemned the operation on Telegram, calling it a cowardly assassination of one of their most significant commanders involved in supervising the October 7 assault.

This event takes place amid an ongoing, US-backed ceasefire that came into effect in October 2025 to halt a two-year war. Although the truce has significantly reduced large-scale combat, regular Israeli strikes have persisted in the territory. The Gaza health ministry reports that over 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began, while the Israeli military has recorded the deaths of seven soldiers and one civilian contractor.

In the broader political landscape, former Israeli army chief Gadi Eisenkot is currently engaged in negotiations to assemble a governing coalition. Meanwhile, caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu remains in charge of ongoing military operations in the region.

stories.title: Princess Kate Joins Prince William in India for Earthshot Prize
stories.summary:
Kate, the Princess of Wales, is traveling to India to join her husband, Prince William, for his annual Earthshot Prize awards. This three-day visit to Mumbai marks her most prominent overseas trip since undergoing preventative chemotherapy for an unspecified form of cancer in 2024. While currently in remission, Kate has noted that her recovery is non-linear and that the illness continues to affect her daily life, leading her to significantly reduce her official workload.

Prince William founded the Earthshot Prize in 2020 to champion climate change solutions, offering five winners £1 million each to expand their projects. Kensington Palace described the initiative as a way to replace pessimism with possibility by highlighting global environmental ingenuity. The upcoming Mumbai awards ceremony is expected to be the largest yet, featuring numerous high-profile guests including Indian cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, actors Alia Bhatt and Rami Malek, and British pop group Take That, who will perform in India for the first time.

Beyond the Earthshot Prize ceremonies, the royal couple will participate in various events connected to Indian cinema, fashion, and cricket. Since her cancer treatment, Kate has gradually increased her public appearances but has not previously accompanied William on foreign trips, with the exception of a two-day solo visit to Italy in May focused on early childhood development.

Prince William, who serves as heir to the throne, shares an environmental focus with his father, King Charles. The royal couple's visit to India underscores both their ongoing commitment to global climate action and Princess Kate's measured return to international royal engagements.

stories.title: Punjab Sets November 15 Sugarcane Crushing Start Amid Mill Association Pushback
stories.summary:
The Punjab government issued an official notification, approved by the Governor of Punjab, directing the province's sugar mills to begin purchasing sugarcane and commencing the crushing season on November 15. Market forces will dictate sugarcane prices, according to official sources. Cultivation data shows that roughly 2.452 million acres were planted with sugarcane this year, representing a 16 percent increase compared to the previous year. Out of 47 registered sugar mills in the region, 41 are currently functional, and the Punjab Food Safety and Consumer Protection Department has assured that farmers' rights will be safeguarded.

The North Zone of the Sugar Mills Association of Pakistan strongly criticized the short-notice directive, arguing that it is impractical to start operations immediately. The association noted that heavy machinery and boilers require approximately two weeks to become fully operational, and under the Sugarcane Act of 1950, mills are permitted to begin operations by November 30. Furthermore, the association highlighted that the government issued the notification at 9 p.m., leaving mills insufficient time to prepare.

Association representatives also raised concerns over existing financial burdens, stating that approximately 1.3 million tonnes of surplus sugar are currently sitting in warehouse inventories. Mills have reportedly paid billions of rupees in taxes and markups on these unsold supplies. Additionally, the association pointed out that out of 300,000 tonnes of government-imported sugar, 100,000 tonnes remain unsold, and criticized the lack of accountability regarding inaccurate official stock figures.

In light of these challenges, the Sugar Mills Association's North Zone has urged the government to clear surplus stocks, permit immediate sugar exports, and fully deregulate the sugar sector. They maintain that crushing cannot safely proceed until the existing surplus is successfully resolved.

stories.title: Chris Pratt and BTS Win Top Honors at Kids' Choice Awards
stories.summary:
The Nickelodeon Kids’ Choice Awards in Los Angeles honored Chris Pratt with the "King of Comedy" title and celebrated South Korean boy band BTS with multiple wins. Hosted by pop singer Alex Warren at Television City, the fan-voted ceremony was broadcast on CBS for the first time alongside its traditional Nickelodeon airing and a live stream on Paramount+ for premium subscribers.

BTS triumphed in three major categories, winning favorite music group for the fifth time, favorite song for "Swim," and favorite album for "ARIRANG." Meanwhile, the film "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" claimed the prize for favorite movie, with its stars Tom Holland and Zendaya taking home the awards for favorite male and female actor, respectively.

Accepting his trophy, Chris Pratt delivered a humorous speech about his four children before shifting to a more serious message emphasizing the importance of appreciating teachers and using comedy to navigate life's challenges. The ceremony also featured live musical performances by Jamie Miller, who sang "Babydoll," and Ashe, who performed "Stop The Wedding!"

The annual event continued its tradition of presenting winners with hollow orange blimp trophies, accompanied by signature slime-filled stunts and celebrity soakings. The broadcast reflects the expanding media portfolio of Skydance, which merged with Paramount in 2025 and subsequently acquired Warner Bros Discovery in October 2026.

stories.title: Saudi-Led Coalition Intercepts Houthi Ballistic Missiles and Drones
stories.summary:
The Saudi-led coalition stated on Sunday that it successfully intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles headed toward the Saudi capital of Riyadh, alongside three drones directed at the kingdom's oil-rich Eastern Province. The incident unfolds amid an escalation of Houthi strikes targeting Saudi infrastructure, which has been met with retaliatory airstrikes by Saudi Arabia against Houthi positions inside Yemen.

The Houthis, who maintain control over the majority of populated areas in Yemen, have recently increased the frequency of their attacks on Riyadh. A prior strike last week impacted an administrative building belonging to state-owned Saudi Aramco located within the financial district of the capital. Meanwhile, the Eastern Province has faced multiple assaults over the past few weeks.

As the economic powerhouse of Saudi Arabia, the Eastern Province holds the vast majority of the nation's oil and natural gas reserves. It also serves as the base for Aramco's headquarters, which sustained substantial damage during a previous attack in October. The ongoing cross-border hostilities continue to target key Saudi facilities, including airports, ports, and oil sites.

The frequent aerial assaults highlight the persistent security challenges facing regional infrastructure. In response to the intensifying campaign by the Houthis, Saudi military forces have ramped up their bombing runs against targets across Yemen, deepening the protracted conflict between the opposing sides.

stories.title: FAA Head Expects US Air Travel to Normalise After Major Outage
stories.summary:
US air travel faced severe nationwide disruptions after a routine maintenance error triggered a massive flight shutdown, with operations expected to stabilise by late Sunday. Federal Aviation Administration head Bryan Bedford announced that the aviation system is gradually recovering from the incident, which prompted a nationwide ground stop lasting nearly five hours on Friday. The stoppage was the longest halt to US air travel since the September 11, 2001 attacks.

According to aviation tracking website FlightAware, airlines had cancelled over 6,400 US flights and delayed more than 8,000 on Saturday, following approximately 9,200 cancellations and 7,500 delays on Friday. Major carriers including Delta Air Lines, United Airlines, and American Airlines cancelled roughly 25% of their schedules on Saturday, while JetBlue cancelled nearly 45%. Airlines provided travel waivers allowing passengers to rebook without additional costs, though tens of thousands of travellers remained stranded in airports.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that the problem stemmed from the installation of at least one new router at a remote facility by FAA contractor L3Harris. The update caused data to overload other communications networks, creating instability in radar and communication systems across 17 of the FAA's 22 en route centers. Officials launched an investigation into whether the incident involved user error or faulty equipment. The White House convened an emergency meeting in the Situation Room on Friday to rule out a cyberattack.

The widespread disruption underscored existing vulnerabilities in the US air traffic control system, which suffers from aging technology and a shortage of controllers. Following the outage, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called for $50 billion in funding to upgrade the infrastructure. Meanwhile, congressional leaders from both parties pledged to hold the administration accountable to prevent a recurrence of the chaos.

stories.title: اسرائیلی فوج کا غزہ میں حماس کمانڈر کی ہلاکت کا دعویٰ
stories.summary:
اسرائیلی فوج نے غزہ میں ایک فضائی حملے کے دوران حماس کے عسکری ونگ کے ایک سینئر کمانڈر کو نشانہ بنانے کا دعویٰ کیا ہے، جبکہ حماس کے ذرائع کے مطابق خان یونس میں ہونے والے اس حملے میں سمیر ابو یونس ہلاک ہوئے ہیں۔ دوسری جانب اسرائیل کے سابق وزیراعظم بنیامین نیتن یاہو نے ایک قومی اتحاد کی حکومت بنانے کی پیشکش کی ہے جسے گادی آئزنکوٹ نے مسترد کرتے ہوئے ایک سیاسی چال قرار دیا ہے۔

نیتن یاہو نے دعویٰ کیا ہے کہ یہ مجوزہ حکومت ایرانی خطرے کا مستقل خاتمہ کر سکتی ہے اور اس میں صرف وہ جماعتیں شامل ہوں گی جو اسرائیل کو یہودی ریاست تسلیم کرتی ہیں۔ یاد رہے کہ گادی آئزنکوٹ کو اتوار 8 نومبر کو نئی حکومت تشکیل دینے کی ذمہ داری سونپی گئی تھی اور انہیں 28 دن کا وقت دیا گیا ہے۔

اس دوران خطے میں سکیورٹی کشیدگی کے تناظر میں بحرین کی وزارتِ داخلہ نے شہریوں کو محتاط رہنے کی ہدایت کی ہے۔ سعودی عرب کے فوجی اتحاد نے بھی مشرقی سعودی عرب اور دارالحکومت ریاض کی جانب داغے جانے والے ایک حوثی ڈرون اور دو بیلسٹک میزائلوں کو فضا میں ہی تباہ کرنے کا اعلان کیا ہے۔

اٹلی کے ڈیٹا تحفظ کے ادارے نے صارفین کی تصاویر اور ویڈیوز تک رضامندی کے بغیر رسائی پر سوشل میڈیا کمپنی میٹا پر 805 ملین یورو کا جرمانہ عائد کیا ہے۔ اطالوی ریگولیٹر کے مطابق فیس بک ایپ کے ایک فیچر کے ذریعے صارفین کو واضح طور پر آگاہ کیے بغیر ان کی گیلری کے مواد کا استعمال کیا جا رہا تھا، تاہم میٹا نے اس فیصلے کے خلاف اپیل کرنے کا اعلان کیا ہے۔

stories.title: نیوزی لینڈ کی خاتون کو 42 برس بعد زندہ بچے کی ای میل موصول
stories.summary:
نیوزی لینڈ سے تعلق رکھنے والی 63 سالہ جانوروں کی ڈاکٹر ڈیان شیہان کو دسمبر 2018 میں ایک نوجوان کی جانب سے موصول ہونے والی ای میل نے حیران کر دیا۔ اس نوجوان نے اپنی تاریخ پیدائش اور ہسپتال کا ذکر کرتے ہوئے لکھا کہ اسے یقین ہے کہ ڈیان اس کی ماں ہیں۔ دلچسپ بات یہ ہے کہ 1976 میں سڈنی کے اسی ہسپتال میں بچے کو جنم دینے کے بعد ڈیان کو بتایا گیا تھا کہ ان کا بچہ مر چکا ہے۔

ڈیان 1950 کی دہائی میں ویلنگٹن کے ایک قدامت پسند کیتھولک خاندان میں پیدا ہوئیں اور جوانی میں آسٹریلیا اور کینیڈا کے دوران رک نامی نوجوان سے ان کے تعلقات استوار ہوئے تھے۔ جب وہ حاملہ ہوئیں تو اس دور کے سماجی دباؤ اور غیر شادی شدہ ماؤں کے خلاف روایتی تعصبات کی وجہ سے انہوں نے حمل کو چھپائے رکھا اور اکیلے ہی سڈنی کے ایک کلینک اور پھر ہسپتال پہنچیں۔

ہسپتال میں عملے نے مبینہ طور پر انہیں شدید صدمے کی حالت میں رکھا، بچے کو بغیر دکھائے الگ کر دیا اور بعد میں اسے مردہ قرار دے دیا تھا۔ اس واقعے کے بعد ڈیان نے کبھی اپنے خاندان، شوہر یا بعد میں پیدا ہونے والے دو بچوں کو اس سچ کے بارے میں نہیں بتایا اور اپنی زندگی جانوروں کے علاج میں مصروف کر دی۔

تحقیقات سے یہ بات سامنے آئی کہ ڈیان ان ہزاروں خواتین میں شامل تھیں جو 1950 سے 1970 کی دہائیوں کے دوران آسٹریلیا میں جبری گود لینے کے نظام کا نشانہ بنی تھیں۔ آسٹریلوی حکومت نے 2013 میں اس پالیسی کا اعتراف کرتے ہوئے باضابطہ طور پر متاثرہ خاندانوں سے معافی مانگی تھی، اور 42 سال بعد ملنے والی اس ای میل نے ڈیان کے پرانے زخم دوبارہ تازہ کر دیے۔

stories.title: Peshawar Court Seeks to Declare Sohail Afridi Proclaimed Offender
stories.summary:
An anti-terrorism court in Peshawar has initiated proceedings to declare dysfunctional Chief Minister Sohail Afridi a proclaimed offender in the May 2023 Radio Pakistan attack case. Judge Wali Mohammad Khan issued the order after a detective foot constable reported that Mr. Afridi and Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf activist Mohammad Amir Khan could not be traced. The court directed that proclamation notices under Section 87 of the Code of Criminal Procedure be issued and set November 24 for further proceedings.

The case stems from the ransacking and torching of the Radio Pakistan building in Peshawar during violent protests in May 2023. A supplementary charge-sheet submitted last month named Mr. Afridi, Mohammad Amir Khan, former provincial ministers Taimoor Saleem Khan and Kamran Bangash, and PTI Peshawar president Irfan Saleem as accused. The prosecution's expansion of the case followed forensic video matching by the Punjab Forensic Science Agency and National Database and Registration Authority profile checks.

Mr. Afridi has not been seen publicly since the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on October 11. While his exact whereabouts remain unconfirmed, government officials previously stated he was in preventive custody, and his detention was challenged in the Peshawar High Court by his brother, Amir Khan. Meanwhile, the three other newly nominated co-accused appeared before the court and successfully secured interim pre-arrest bail.

The ongoing trial involves 75 total accused individuals, including current and former lawmakers. The original first information report was lodged at the East Cantonment police station on May 10, 2023, by station house officer Arbab Naeem Haider under the Pakistan Penal Code and Anti-Terrorism Act. The newly implicated individuals have contested the authenticity of the forensic video evidence linking them to the riots.

stories.title: US Diesel Prices Drop Below Six Dollars After Two Months
stories.summary:
Average US retail diesel prices fell below six dollars a gallon on Saturday, dropping to $5.998 according to data from fuel price tracker GasBuddy. This decline marks the first time prices have fallen under this threshold in two months, offering relief after diesel surged due to disruptions from the US-Israeli conflict with Iran and Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries.

Elevated fuel expenses had significantly driven up overall inflation, impacting transportation costs for consumers, farmers, and businesses. High costs also served as a major factor in the Democratic sweep of both houses of Congress during this month's midterm elections against President Donald Trump’s Republican party. National diesel prices previously broke previous records on September 3 and reached a peak of $6.519 on September 22, while California prices briefly exceeded ten dollars a gallon.

In response to the crisis, the Trump administration implemented several interventions, including temporarily waiving federal taxes on red-dyed diesel, relaxing sanctions on Russian fuel, and deploying an eight billion dollar support initiative for farmers during the autumn harvest. However, these measures provided limited initial relief while ongoing supply anxieties related to the war in Iran persisted across the market.

Current price reductions are primarily driven by seasonal demand drops and falling crude oil values, with Brent crude futures down 18.5 percent over two weeks. Patrick De Haan, GasBuddy's head of petroleum analysis, noted that autumn demand typically softens alongside completed refinery maintenance and a reduced risk of Gulf Coast hurricane disruptions, which also pushed gasoline below four dollars a gallon this month.

stories.title: Bahrain Issues Security Alerts Amid Regional Tensions
stories.summary:
Bahrain's interior ministry issued two separate social media alerts on the platform X on Sunday, warning citizens and residents of potential threats and urging them to remain calm while moving to the nearest safe location. These advisories mark the first warnings issued by the Gulf nation since September.

The precautionary statements followed a claim by Iran's Revolutionary Guards asserting they had targeted a US early-warning radar stationed in Bahrain. The United States military promptly disputed this assertion, reporting that it successfully intercepted two incoming Iranian drones without sustaining any damage or casualties.

Bahrain hosts the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet, placing the island nation in a sensitive strategic position amid heightened regional frictions. The security alerts also coincided with a reported seafarer fatality resulting from a suspected missile strike targeting an oil tanker operating within the Gulf region.

stories.title: لاہور دنیا اور بہاولپور پاکستان کا سب سے آلودہ شہر قرار
stories.summary:
عالمی ماحولیاتی ویب سائٹ کے اعداد و شمار کے مطابق لاہور دنیا بھر کے تمام شہروں میں فضائی آلودگی کے لحاظ سے پہلے نمبر پر ریکارڈ کیا گیا ہے۔ شہر میں آلودگی کے ذرات کی تعداد 235 تک جا پہنچی، جبکہ بھارت کا شہر کولکتہ 227 ذرات کے ساتھ فہرست میں دوسرے مقام پر رہا۔

لاہور کے مختلف علاقوں میں بھی فضائی آلودگی کی شرح انتہائی بلند ریکارڈ کی گئی۔ اس سلسلے میں سی آر پی آفس گلبرگ میں ذرات کی تعداد 298 اور برکی روڈ پر 291 درج کی گئی۔ اس کے علاوہ کینٹ میں 264، اقبال ٹاؤن میں 239، ماڈل ٹاؤن میں 230، ڈیفنس میں 214 اور عسکری 10 میں آلودگی کے ذرات 167 ریکارڈ کیے گئے۔

دوسری جانب ملک بھر کے آلودہ ترین شہروں کا جائزہ لیا جائے تو پنجاب کا شہر بہاولپور 426 ذرات کی ریکارڈ تعداد کے ساتھ پاکستان بھر میں پہلے نمبر پر آگیا ہے۔ فضائی آلودگی کی یہ تشویشناک صورتحال شہریوں کی صحت کے لیے شدید خطرات پیدا کر رہی ہے اور متعلقہ اداروں کے لیے ایک بڑا چیلنج بن چکی ہے۔

اس ماحول میں فضائی آلودگی کی بڑھتی ہوئی شرح سے بچاؤ کے لیے حکومتی اقدامات اور شہریوں کی احتیاطی تدابیر انتہائی ضروری ہو چکی ہیں۔ ماہرین صحت شہریوں کو غیر ضروری سفر سے گریز کرنے اور ماسک استعمال کرنے کا مشورہ دے رہے ہیں تاکہ اس مضر صحت ماحول کے منفی اثرات سے محفوظ رہا جا سکے۔

stories.title: ترک نائب وزیرِ خارجہ اقتصادی تعاون تنظیم کے اجلاس کیلئے اسلام آباد پہنچ گئے
stories.summary:
ترکیہ کے نائب وزیرِ خارجہ موسیٰ کُلالکلکیا اقتصادی تعاون تنظیم (ECO) کے وزرائے خارجہ کونسل کے اجلاس میں شرکت کے لیے دارالحکومت اسلام آباد پہنچ گئے ہیں۔ موصوف اس اہم اجلاس میں ترک وفد کی مکمل قیادت کریں گے۔

سفارتی ذرائع کے مطابق اس اعلیٰ سطحی وزرائے خارجہ اجلاس میں ایران کے وزیرِ خارجہ عباس عراقچی بھی خصوصی طور پر شرکت کریں گے۔ تاہم سفارتی سطح پر یہ بات بھی سامنے آئی ہے کہ افغان وزیرِ خارجہ کو اس اجلاس میں شرکت کی کوئی دعوت نہیں دی گئی۔

اجلاس کے باضابطہ آغاز سے قبل، تنظیم کے سیکریٹریز اور تمام فوکل نمائندگان اسلام آباد میں سرگرم ہو چکے ہیں۔ یہ نمائندگان وزرائے خارجہ کے اگلے روز ہونے والے اہم اجلاس کا مکمل ایجنڈا طے کرنے کے فرائض سر انجام دے رہے ہیں۔

اس خطے میں باہمی تعاون، سفارتی روابط اور اقتصادی ترقی کے تناظر میں یہ اجلاس انتہائی اہمیت کا حامل سمجھا جا رہا ہے۔ اس کے ذریعے رکن ممالک کے درمیان مختلف شعبوں میں اشتراکِ کار کو مزید فروغ دینے کی راہیں تلاش کی جائیں گی جو کہ خطے کے مستقبل کے لیے بہت اہم ہے۔

stories.title: Philippines and Australia Sign New Defence Cooperation Arrangement
stories.summary:
The Philippines and Australia formally signed a defence cooperation arrangement on Sunday designed to simplify administrative procedures for joint military engagements. Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro stated that the agreement serves as an anti-red tape measure to streamline the execution of the bilateral Status of Visiting Forces Agreement, reducing coordination steps significantly.

Secretary Teodoro noted that the pact will facilitate expanded collaboration across maritime, air, and land forces, as well as humanitarian and disaster relief operations. He emphasized that the deal strengthens Manila's credible deterrence posture, particularly regarding territorial disputes in the South China Sea. The Philippines has actively expanded its security partnerships alongside its primary alliance with the United States to counter what it terms aggressive Chinese maritime activities.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese attended the signing ceremony in Manila during an Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit. Albanese highlighted that the agreement will improve maritime domain awareness, boost intelligence sharing, and expand strategic dialogue, joint training, and defence infrastructure development. He additionally committed new Australian investments toward maritime drone technology, equipment, and training to counter regional security threats.

Beijing consistently opposes joint military drills between Manila and its allies, arguing that such activities escalate regional tensions. Meanwhile, Australia continues to support the Philippines' stance in the strategic waterway, backing a 2016 international arbitral tribunal ruling that rejected China's expansive territorial claims under international law—a decision that Beijing rejects as unlawful.

stories.title: اسلام آباد میں اقتصادی تعاون تنظیم کے سیکریٹریز کا اجلاس شروع
stories.summary:
اقتصادی تعاون تنظیم (ECO) کے سیکریٹریز اور فوکل نمائندگان کا اہم اجلاس باضابطہ طور پر اسلام آباد میں شروع ہو چکا ہے۔ اس اجلاس میں خطے کے کئی اہم امور پر غور و خوض کیا جا رہا ہے۔

اجلاس کا بنیادی مقصد اگلے روز منعقد ہونے والے وزرائے خارجہ کے اجلاس کے لیے تفصیلی ایجنڈا طے کرنا ہے۔ سفارتی ذرائع نے تصدیق کی ہے کہ وزرائے خارجہ کے اس آئندہ اجلاس میں ایران کے وزیرِ خارجہ عباس عراقچی خصوصی طور پر شریک ہوں گے، جبکہ افغان وزیرِ خارجہ کو شرکت کی دعوت نہیں دی گئی ہے۔

موجودہ اجلاس کے دوران علاقائی تجارت کے فروغ، ٹرانسپورٹ کے نظام کی بہتری اور توانائی کے مختلف شعبوں میں باہمی تعاون بڑھانے پر بات چیت کی جا رہی ہے۔ اس کے علاوہ وسطی ایشیا کے خطے کو عالمی منڈیوں کے ساتھ منسلک کرنے کے ممکنہ طریقوں کا بھی جائزہ لیا جا رہا ہے۔

اس نوعیت کے علاقائی اجلاس خطے کے ممالک کے درمیان اقتصادی اور تجارتی تعلقات کو مضبوط بنانے میں کلیدی کردار ادا کرتے ہیں۔ ان بیٹھکوں کے ذریعے طے پانے والے فیصلے مستقبل میں مشترکہ ترقی اور خوشحالی کی بنیاد بنتے ہیں۔

stories.title: بورے والا: گھریلو ناچاقی پر ماں نے بچوں سمیت زہریلی گولیاں کھالیں
stories.summary:
بورے والا کے نواحی علاقے چک نمبر 315 ای بی میں گھریلو ناچاقی کے باعث ایک دلخراش واقعہ پیش آیا جہاں چالیس سالہ خاتون نے مبینہ طور پر اپنے بچوں کے ہمراہ زہریلی گولیاں کھا لیں۔

واقعے کے نتیجے میں چالیس سالہ خاتون موقع پر ہی دم توڑ گئیں جبکہ بچوں کو تشویشناک حالت میں مقامی اسپتال منتقل کیا گیا۔

اسپتال میں طبی امداد کے بعد گیارہ سالہ بچی کی حالت زیادہ خراب ہونے پر اسے مزید علاج کے لیے ٹیچنگ اسپتال ساہیوال روانہ کر دیا گیا۔

ریسکیو حکام کے مطابق مجموعی طور پر چاروں لڑکیوں کو تشویشناک حالت میں اسپتال منتقل کیا گیا تھا۔ پولیس اس معاملے کی مزید تفتیش کر رہی ہے۔

stories.title: Saudi Arabia Arrests Nearly 12,000 Illegal Residents in Nationwide Crackdown
stories.summary:
Saudi Arabian security forces detained 11,952 individuals during a nationwide enforcement operation conducted between November 5 and 11. The Ministry of Interior reported that the joint inspection campaigns focused on breaches of the Kingdom's residency, border security, and labour regulations. The total number of apprehensions included 6,163 residency law offenders, 3,225 border security violators, and 2,564 labour law breakers. Additionally, authorities intercepted 1,653 people attempting unauthorized entry across the border and 29 individuals trying to leave through illegal routes.

During the same weeklong sweep, 11,418 lawbreakers were deported from the country. Officials also directed 22,451 violators to their respective diplomatic missions for travel documents and instructed 9,800 others to finalize departure arrangements. Furthermore, security forces arrested 15 people suspected of housing, employing, or transporting offenders. Legal proceedings are currently underway for 40,762 expatriates, comprising 38,383 men and 2,379 women.

The Ministry of Interior issued stern warnings regarding the facilitation of illegal entrants or the provision of shelter and transport. Individuals found guilty of assisting violators can face prison sentences of up to 15 years and financial penalties reaching SR1 million, alongside the potential confiscation of properties and vehicles used in the offenses. The ministry urged citizens and residents to report suspicious activities by dialing 911 in Makkah, Riyadh, and the Eastern Province, or 999 and 996 in remaining regions.

stories.title: CPJ Urges US to Release Afghan Journalist Facing Deportation
stories.summary:
The Committee to Protect Journalists has called on US Immigration and Customs Enforcement authorities to immediately and unconditionally release Afghan reporter Shaban Ali Rafat. CPJ also requested that Rafat be granted full access to a hearing regarding his asylum claim. The organization warned that sending Rafat back to Afghanistan would place him in severe danger of persecution and retaliation by the Taliban regime.

Rafat has been held in an ICE facility in California since January 21, 2025, after arriving in the United States to seek refuge. According to his legal representative, David Tarr, the journalist now faces imminent deportation to Afghanistan. CPJ Americas regional program director Jose Zamora emphasized that Rafat fled his home country because Taliban rule made it impossible for him to work safely as a journalist, and returning him would place him directly in the hands of his persecutors.

stories.title: US Socialists Win Major Elections as Party Gains Mainstream Ground
stories.summary:
In the United States, once-stigmatized socialist politics are experiencing a surge as members of the Democratic Socialists of America achieve notable electoral victories. Following November midterm elections, DSA-endorsed politicians secured mayoral offices in major cities including New York and Los Angeles, while expanding their congressional representation from two seats to eight alongside numerous local wins. Observers note that these victories coincided with broader Democratic success following pushback against President Donald Trump’s Republicans.

Founded in 1982 with an initial focus on labor organizing, the DSA maintained a small profile until membership surged past 130,000 following Donald Trump’s first election. The movement gained significant visibility through figures like Senator Bernie Sanders, Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, and Los Angeles Mayor-elect Nithya Raman. While scholars debate whether the socialist label directly drove voter turnout or if general anti-Trump sentiment fueled the broader Democratic wave, polls indicate a rising acceptance of socialist ideas in America.

Mamdani has leveraged progressive platforms addressing affordable housing, healthcare access, and immigrant protections, citing historical inspiration from Milwaukee’s mid-century "sewer socialists." Meanwhile, Raman focused her campaign on local infrastructure and affordability issues. Experts suggest that these successful urban campaigns have normalized socialism, transforming the label into an asset for candidates targeting economic concerns.

Despite the electoral momentum, some political scientists remain cautious. Harvard government professor Stephen Ansolabehere argues that the wins reflect a general rising tide for the Democratic Party rather than a specific mandate for socialism. Georgetown professor Hans Noel similarly notes that DSA-backed candidates succeeded primarily in heavily Democratic areas and primary contests. Nonetheless, the growing cadre of left-wing politicians demonstrates an expanding electoral footprint for the American socialist movement.

stories.title: Middle East Tankers Burn and Spills Spread Despite Hopes
stories.summary:
Despite falling oil prices and expectations of de-escalation, maritime attacks persist in the Middle East, leaving tankers ablaze and oil spills washing ashore in Oman and the United Arab Emirates. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency reported another tanker incident in the Strait of Hormuz on a Wednesday, while Iranian state reports indicated an oil tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine. According to the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, at least 10 ships were hit in the first ten days of November, following 37 attacks in October.

Verified social media videos and European Union satellite imagery revealed a Navig8 tanker burning off the coast of Oman. Iran claimed responsibility for targeting three tankers on the same day for navigating unauthorized routes through the Strait of Hormuz. Concurrently, United States forces continue enforcing a naval blockade on Iranian ports, with US Central Command reporting that a military aircraft fired upon and disabled a St. Kitts-flagged cargo vessel attempting to leave regional waters after a port visit.

The ongoing maritime violence has triggered environmental degradation, with satellite imagery and local video footage confirming oil leaks reaching Omani shores. Beyond the waters, regional energy and civilian infrastructure have also faced strikes. The Iran-backed Houthis launched missile attacks targeting the offices of Saudi Aramco in Riyadh, causing limited debris damage without injuries or fatalities, as confirmed by the Saudi Energy Ministry and verified video footage.

Since the conflict began in late February, the International Maritime Organization has documented 133 incidents, predominantly attacks, resulting in the deaths of at least 25 seafarers. The continued bombardment of shipping lanes and infrastructure underscores the persistent volatility in the region despite preliminary economic indicators suggesting potential cooling.

stories.title: Lucky Motor Suspends Peugeot 2008 Bookings Amid Market Shifts
stories.summary:
Lucky Motor Corporation has suspended fresh bookings for the Peugeot 2008 in Pakistan, four years after launching the European SUV as a locally assembled model in early 2022. The vehicle, which was assembled at the Port Bin Qasim Industrial Park with over 6,000 units produced since its debut, has struggled following a shift in consumer demand toward electrified vehicles triggered by rising petrol prices after the Middle East conflict began in February. LMC Chief Executive Muhammad Faisal confirmed the suspension of new orders to Dawn, though he denied rumors that the assembly line had been completely shut down, stating that existing orders are still being fulfilled and parts remain in stock.

The slowdown in demand for petrol-only models has impacted other manufacturers as well, prompting Honda Atlas Cars to discontinue the BR-V. In response to market pressures, LMC slashed prices across its lineup, reducing the Peugeot 2008 Active from Rs6.999 million to Rs5.799 million and the Allure variant from Rs7.799 million to Rs6.499 million. Prices for its Kia Sportage HEV models were also significantly cut. However, market sources and upcountry dealers provided conflicting accounts regarding production status, and at least one former authorized showroom on Rashid Minhas Road in Karachi, Macca Motors, was found rebranded to display vehicles from Chinese brand GAC.

Used car owners praised the Peugeot 2008 for its driving comfort, aesthetics, and durability, but highlighted severe drawbacks including high running costs, low fuel economy of 8 to 8.5 kilometers per litre, and poor resale value. Existing owners expressed frustration over a lack of communication from LMC regarding future support and parts availability. Meanwhile, LMC continues its operations with other models, maintaining the Kia Sportage while evaluating the feasibility of newer generations following its partnership agreements with Stellantis and China’s Guangzhou Automobile Group.

stories.title: کراچی کی تاریخی شناخت، پرانے نام اور بدلتے ہوئے شہری نقوش
stories.summary:
پاکستان کا سب سے بڑا شہر کراچی طویل عرصے سے مختلف برادریوں اور مذاہب کا گہوارہ رہا ہے، جہاں لوگ باہمی احترام کے ساتھ رہتے تھے۔ وقت کے ساتھ ساتھ اس کے شہری نقوش اور سڑکوں کے ناموں میں نمایاں تبدیلیاں آ چکی ہیں۔ آزادی سے پہلے بہت سے مقامات کے نام ہندو شخصیات یا خاندانوں سے منسوب تھے، جو بعد میں تبدیل کر دیے گئے۔ رنچھوڑ لائن اور رام سوامی جیسے تاریخی علاقے اب بھی اپنے پرانے ناموں سے جانے جاتے ہیں، جبکہ ان کی گلیوں اور مارکیٹوں کی تاریخ مقامی محققین نے محفوظ کی ہے۔

رنچھوڑ لائن کا نام کچھھی ہندو تاجر رنچھوڑ داس کے نام پر پڑا، جنہوں نے یہاں مکانات تعمیر کیے تھے۔ اس علاقے کے آس پاس کی کئی گلیاں ہندو شخصیات کے نام پر تھیں، جیسے نارائن پورہ اور ہیرالال اسٹریٹ، جبکہ 1899 کا پونا بھائی ٹاور اور 1926 کی ہوتی مارکیٹ آج بھی اس کی پہچان ہیں۔ حکومت نے اس علاقے کا نام بدل کر گزدر آباد بھی رکھا تھا، لیکن عوامی سطح پر پرانی شناخت ہی برقرار رہی۔

رام سوامی کا علاقہ سووامی نارائن فرقے کے ہندوؤں کی آبادی کی وجہ سے معروف ہوا۔ یہیں تلسی داس اسٹریٹ تھی جسے کثرتِ درختوں کی وجہ سے جھاڑ والی گلی بھی کہا جاتا تھا۔ اسی علاقے میں 1893 میں بنی اسرائیل سینیگاگ نامی یہودیوں کی عبادت گاہ قائم تھی، جو بعد میں منہدم کر دی گئی۔ کراچی کے قدیم میوہ شاہ قبرستان میں ایک یہودی قبرستان بھی موجود ہے جہاں لگ بھگ پانچ سو قبریں واقع ہیں۔

شہر کے پرانے علاقوں میں گاندھی گارڈن بھی خاص اہمیت رکھتا ہے جو پہلے وکٹوریہ گارڈن کہلاتا تھا اور 1934 میں مہاتما گاندھی کی آمد پر اس کا نام تبدیل کیا گیا۔ ان تاریخی تبدیلیوں اور یادوں کے باوجود کراچی کے پرانے علاقوں کی ثقافتی وسعت اور رونقیں بزرگ شہریوں کی یادوں اور تاریخی کتابوں میں اب بھی زندہ ہیں۔

stories.title: Pakistan Emerges as an Asymmetric Middle Power Amid Regional Crises
stories.summary:
As the global order shifts toward fragmented multipolarity, middle powers are playing a vital role as diplomatic bridges and economic shock absorbers. Scholars evaluate middle power status across three pillars: military capability, diplomatic outreach, and comprehensive national strength driven by economic and technological vitality. Over recent years, Pakistan has leveraged its military strength and active diplomacy to re-enter global strategic relevance, though its foundational economic pillar remains weak, rendering its emerging status fragile.

Pakistan’s hard-power credentials were underscored during a four-day conflict with India in May 2025, featuring aerial clashes and precision missile exchanges. Operation Bunyanum Marsoos demonstrated modern warfare capabilities, compelling a White House-facilitated ceasefire on May 10 and reinforcing Islamabad’s deterrence. Translating battlefield credibility into security partnerships, Pakistan signed the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia in September 2025, joined the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkey in August 2026, and entered the Badr agreement alongside Qatar, Turkey, and Indonesia.

Diplomatically, Pakistan adopted a posture of active neutrality following the outbreak of US-Israeli military hostilities against Iran in early 2026. Acting as a primary conduit to Tehran, Islamabad hosted peace talks in April 2026 and helped secure a memorandum of understanding in June to temporarily reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Pakistan also joined Donald Gaza peace plan as a founding member, expanding its diplomatic footprint beyond its borders.

Despite these military and diplomatic milestones, severe domestic economic deficits threaten Pakistan's middle power aspirations. While FY2025-26 indicators showed surface stabilization with 3.7 percent GDP growth and 7 to 9 percent inflation, investment hovers near 15 percent of GDP—far below the threshold required to support a booming youth population. Deindustrialization, high energy costs, low tax-to-GDP ratios, external debt servicing, and reliance on remittances and bailouts constrain economic autonomy. Analysts argue that without an urgent domestic economic pivot to foster industrial competitiveness and technological innovation, Islamabad’s geopolitical leverage will remain vulnerable to shifting global priorities.

stories.title: Zelenskyy Says US Proposed Ukraine Cede Territory for NATO Membership
stories.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy disclosed that Washington suggested Kyiv cede land in exchange for joining NATO, marking the first time the proposition has been raised. Zelenskyy made the remarks in comments released on Saturday following high-level discussions in Abu Dhabi between US envoys Jared Kushner, Steve Witkoff, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Ukrainian officials, which ended without a breakthrough.

The diplomatic talks did yield an agreement for European nations to participate in future negotiations to end the ongoing war. In Dublin, European officials selected five countries—France, Germany, Italy, the UK, and Poland—to send representatives. Despite the Western defense support strengthening Ukraine's army, Zelenskyy emphasized that Kyiv would not recognize any territory seized by Moscow and would consult Ukrainian citizens before agreeing to any proposals.

The prospect of Ukraine joining NATO remains a core point of contention. Russia launched its 2022 invasion citing Western plans to incorporate Ukraine into the alliance, viewing NATO membership as a red line. Meanwhile, Kremlin representatives have rejected wider ceasefires and an energy ceasefire, with Moscow's chief negotiator Vladimir Medinsky stating that the Kremlin aims for a modern Yalta conference to reshape European security.

Zelenskyy also warned against a Russian proposal for a humanitarian mission in the contested eastern town of Kostyantynivka, arguing it is a ploy to force a Ukrainian withdrawal and open paths to other cities in the Donetsk region. As the winter military campaign intensifies, Zelenskyy noted that Ukraine is concurrently pursuing specific post-war security guarantees from Western countries to secure its army's future.

stories.title: US Aviation Head Predicts Flight Operations Will Normalize Sunday
stories.summary:
US air travel disruptions are expected to persist until late Sunday, Federal Aviation Administration head Bryan Bedford announced, as the aviation system slowly recovers from a historic nationwide flight shutdown. The massive disruption stemmed from routine maintenance gone awry when an FAA contractor, L3Harris, installed at least one new router at a remote facility in Arkansas or Texas. The technical fault caused data overloads and instability in radar and communications systems across 17 of the FAA's 22 en route centers.

Friday's crisis forced the FAA to order a nationwide ground stop that halted nearly all departing flights for almost five hours. It marked the longest national halt to US air travel since the attacks of September 11, 2001. By Saturday evening, flight tracking website FlightAware reported that airlines had canceled more than 6,400 US flights and delayed over 8,000, with an additional 875 Sunday flights already scrapped. Major carriers including Delta, United, American Airlines, and JetBlue canceled a substantial percentage of their schedules, leaving tens of thousands of passengers stranded.

The White House convened an emergency Situation Room meeting on Friday to rule out a cyberattack. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that officials are investigating whether the incident resulted from user or installer error by L3Harris or a faulty router. The Professional Aviation Safety Specialists union noted that its technicians were not involved in the router updates.

In response to the crisis, Transportation Secretary Duffy called for $50 billion in funding to upgrade aging air traffic control technology and equipment. House Speaker Mike Johnson expressed support for increased aviation funding this year. Meanwhile, congressional Democrats slated to lead transport committees next year vowed to hold the administration accountable to prevent future system collapses.

stories.title: SpaceX Starship Orbiting Earth Safely After Booster Catch Aborted
stories.summary:
SpaceX's Starship spacecraft remained healthy while orbiting Earth on Saturday, tracking toward a planned return to its Texas launch site following its 15th test flight. The ambitious mission was originally designed to achieve a historic twin recovery of both the Super Heavy booster and the Starship spacecraft using mechanical launch tower arms, marking a crucial step toward fully reusable rocket systems.

Minutes after liftoff from Starbase on Friday afternoon, the twin-stage rocket executed stage separation. However, the Super Heavy booster experienced a guidance, navigation, and control (GNC) issue near the end of its descent. According to SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot, the booster aborted itself and diverted to the Gulf of Mexico, where it automatically self-destructed before hitting the water. Despite this setback, the Starship upper stage successfully reached orbit and deployed 26 satellites for Elon Musk's Starlink constellation.

Aerospace experts described the mission as a mixed bag due to the loss of the Super Heavy booster, which SpaceX had successfully caught three times previously. NASA continues to rely on Starship as a lunar lander for its Artemis missions, with NASA administrator Jared Isaacman congratulating SpaceX on the launch. Unlike the booster, the Starship spacecraft was slated to complete 14 orbits before returning to Earth after more than 22 hours of flight for a highly complex recovery attempt.

stories.title: SpaceX Starship Aces Re-entry and Lands in Tower Mechanical Arms
stories.summary:
SpaceX's Starship spacecraft successfully returned from a 22.5-hour orbital journey on Saturday, executing a precision landing into the grasp of giant mechanical arms at its Starbase launch site in Texas. The milestone achievement brings billionaire Elon Musk's company closer to developing a fully reusable rocket system designed to reduce mission costs and operate with the frequency of commercial aircraft.

During the mission's 15th test flight, the towering two-stage rocket lifted off on Friday, deploying 26 Starlink satellites into orbit at an altitude of roughly 161 miles. While the Super Heavy booster failed to return to the launch pad shortly after liftoff, the Starship upper stage completed its orbital objectives. On Saturday, Starship initiated an atmospheric plunge over the Pacific Ocean, decelerating from 17,000 miles per hour while enduring intense thermal re-entry heat. As it descended through thick clouds above south Texas, the charred spacecraft reignited its engines, flipped vertical, and was successfully caught by the tower's 'Mechazilla' arms.

Musk and SpaceX engineers inspected the vehicle shortly after the catch, with Musk sharing photos and videos of 'Ship 42' online. SpaceX has spent more than $15 billion developing Starship, alongside $3.2 billion in funding from NASA's $4 billion Artemis contract aimed at returning humans to the moon by 2028. Future development milestones for Starship include demonstrating complex orbital fuel transfers between tanker rockets to enable deep-space missions beyond Earth's orbit.

stories.title: US Aviation System Hit by Five-Hour Ground Stop After Router Malfunction
stories.summary:
A massive, nearly five-hour shutdown of the United States aviation system disrupted over 20,000 flights starting Friday, with government officials reporting on Saturday that the failure may stem from a single router installed by government contractor L3Harris. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that L3Harris was performing routine maintenance to transition communication lines from old copper wires to fiber at remote locations. Officials noted potential router issues in both Arkansas and Texas.

The incident highlighted ongoing struggles within the aging Federal Aviation Administration telecommunication network. Duffy noted that the newly installed routers began flooding other systems with more than 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, causing data instability and communication issues with planes and radar at 17 of the FAA's 22 en route centers nationwide. The agency enacted a nationwide ground stop because it could not immediately identify the root cause.
